name: Hu & Verdaguer: divergences do occur in the coincidence limit

source.located: arXiv:0802.0658v1 [gr-qc] 5 Feb 2008, B.L. Hu & E. Verdaguer, 'Stochastic Gravity: Theory and Applications' (Feb 2008 update of the 2003 Living Review; Living Rev. Rel. 11 (2008) 3). Sec. 5.2.1 'Finiteness of Noise Kernel', p.29-30, Eqs. (5.17)-(5.22); context Sec. 3.2 p.10 (Eqs. 3.11-3.13), Sec. 5 intro p.24-25, Sec. 5.2 p.27-28 (Eqs. 5.9-5.13), Sec. 5.2.2 p.30-32 (Eqs. 5.26-5.32), p.80 (horizon-smeared remark). Primary source of the Sec. 5.2.1 text: Phillips & Hu gr-qc/0010019v2 (Phys. Rev. D 63, 104001 (2001)) Sec. III.A p.9-10, Sec. II p.6, Sec. V p.18.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 0802.0658 (two calls) returned pp.1, 8, 10, 24-32, 80, 84, 88, 92 verbatim; alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/0010019 returned pp.1-2, 5-6, 9-10, 13, 15-16, 18. The Sec. 5.2.1 paragraph of the review is word-for-word Phillips & Hu 2001 Sec. III.A.

published_statement: 0802.0658 Sec. 5.2.1 p.29: 'Since T_ab(x) defined at one point can be ill-behaved as it is generally divergent, one can question the soundness of these quantities. But as will be shown later, the noise kernel is finite for y != x. All field operator products present in the first expectation value that could be divergent are canceled by similar products in the second term. ... Wick's theorem will allow the four point functions to be re-expressed in terms of two point functions. From this we see that all possible divergences for y != x will cancel. When the coincidence limit is taken divergences do occur. The above procedure will allow us to isolate the divergences and obtain a finite result.' p.25: N(x,y) 'is always finite for x != y (and off the light cone for massless theories)'; the review sets 'a more modest goal ... and leave the discussion of point-wise limit to a later date'. Sec. 3.2 p.10: 'The noise kernel should be thought of as a distribution function, the limit of coincidence points has meaning only in the sense of distributions.' Primary (Phillips & Hu gr-qc/0010019 p.6): 'Of course, without use of a regularized Green function, the y -> x limit is divergent'; p.18: 'The noise kernel as a two point function of the stress energy tensor diverges as the pair of points are brought together, representing the "standard" ultraviolet divergence'.
published_hypotheses: H1 free (linear) scalar field, mass m, curvature coupling xi, action (3.1); stress tensor (5.9)/(5.10) (p.27-28)

H2 Wick's theorem for the 4-point function: 'for the case of free fields which we are considering' (p.30, Eq. 5.20) -- i.e. a quasi-free (Gaussian) state; the review and Phillips-Hu call N the 'vacuum expectation value' of the bi-tensor (abstract; PH p.2)

H3 physically acceptable = Hadamard states for the renormalised T^R (Sec. 3.1, p.8); the 'finite result' after isolating divergences uses modified point separation, subtracting a Hadamard ansatz (PH Sec. IV)
H4 point pairs (x,x') and (y,y') each in a Riemann normal neighbourhood; for y -> x all four points in one such neighbourhood (p.30)
H5 finiteness for x != y requires, for massless theories, x,y off the light cone (p.25)
H6 the 'divergences do occur' sentence is an ASSERTION in the review (the pointwise limit is explicitly deferred, p.25); no divergence coefficient is computed in 0802.0658
hypothesis_drift: NONE DROPPED on the load-bearing hypothesis: noise.py:206-207 applies the sentence to the coincidence limit of the linear-field noise kernel, and the file keeps H1 elsewhere (noise.py:202 'for a linear field'; noise.py:222-224 refuses nonminimal coupling and interacting fields, 'H1 is essential').

CHARACTERISATION, not drift (noise.py:206): the tree says the Sec. 3.2 quote 'is about SEPARATED points'. Sec. 3.2 does not say 'separated points'; it says the kernel is free of UV divergences because the c-number counterterms cancel and then qualifies: 'the limit of coincidence points has meaning only in the sense of distributions' (p.10). The tree's gloss is consistent with that qualification and with Sec. 5.2.1/p.25 ('finite for x != y'); a more exact wording would be 'as a distribution / at separated points'.

OMITTED CONTEXT (noise.py:206-207): the source's next sentence, 'The above procedure will allow us to isolate the divergences and obtain a finite result', is not carried. The finite coincident result H&V/PH mean is obtained by Hadamard SUBTRACTION (PH Sec. IV, Eq. 4.10) -- a regularisation of the pointwise kernel. Its omission does not bias the tree: it supports the tree's narrowing that the POINTWISE coincidence object needs more than the Sec. 3.2 counterterm cancellation, while the tree's own finiteness route (worldline smearing, Fewster 1208.5399 Sec. 3.3) is a different one and is left NAMED (noise.py:207-211, 275).
NOT CARRIED, harmless: H4 (normal neighbourhoods) and H5 (off the light cone for massless fields) -- they concern finiteness at separated points, not the coincidence divergence the tree cites.

STATUS WORD: noise.py:206 'H&V Sec. 5.2.1 say' -- accurate; the tree does not claim H&V demonstrated the divergence (H6), and noise.py:371 records 'page text, Secs. 3.2, 5.2.1', which matches what was read.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (exit 0; output saved at rederive/0802.0658-sec5.2.1.out). C1: a c-number counterterm F*I cancels in t = T - <T> (the Sec. 3.2 mechanism). C2: H&V's explicit functional, Eqs. (5.26),(5.29)-(5.32) at R=0, m=0, general xi, evaluated on the Minkowski-vacuum Wightman function, equals an independent Wick-theorem evaluation of the connected <T_ab(x)T_cd(y)> from the stress tensor (5.9) on 8 components (difference exactly 0). (The mirror term N~_c'd' is not printed on the pages read; it was taken as the x<->y mirror of (5.31).) C3: N_0000 is proportional to C_0000 = 3(30 xi^2 - 10 xi + 1)/(2 pi^4 r^8) at equal-time separation r and the same coefficient over tau^8 along a timelike worldline; the quadratic has discriminant -20, so the coefficient is nonzero for EVERY real xi (3/(2 pi^4) at xi=0, 1/(4 pi^4) at xi=1/6) -- the pointwise y -> x limit diverges, and r^-8 is not locally integrable in 3-space or along a line (the kernel exists only as a distribution, the Sec. 3.2 sentence). C4: with the Wightman i*eps rule the worldline-smeared double integral equals (1/7!) int_0^oo w^7 |f^(w)|^2 dw (checked to 1e-15 at eps = 0.7, 0.3) and is finite at eps -> 0 (= 48/(7! tau^8) = 1/105 for tau = 1, Gaussian sampling); without i*eps the cut-off integral grows as delta^-7 (ratio 1.007e7 between delta = 1e-2 and 1e-1). SCOPE: flat space, vacuum, m = 0. The curved Hadamard case is NOT computed here: its leading singularity is the universal Hadamard term, so the r^-8 leading divergence is expected to be state-independent -- an argument NAMED, not run. DISCREPANCY RECORDED (not an error, does not touch the divergence): the review's Sec. 3.2 normalisation, Eq. (3.11) N = (1/2)<{t,t}>, and its Sec. 5 normalisation, Eq. (5.17) 8N = <{t,t}> i.e. N = (1/8)<{t,t}>, differ by a factor 4, although Sec. 5.2.1 introduces its N as 'the noise kernel introduced in Eq. (3.11)'; C2 confirms Sec. 5's functional is internally consistent with (5.17). The Sec. 5 convention is Phillips & Hu's, gr-qc/0010019 Eq. (1.3): 4N = (1/2)<{t,t}>.

later_literature.ref: Perez & Sudarsky, arXiv:2512.17789v2 (Jan 2026), Renormalization of the Quantum Stress Tensor Fluctuations and the Limits of Semiclassical Gravity
later_literature.what: For the coincident <T_ab(x)T_cd(x)> of a free scalar in Hadamard states, 'subtracting a state-independent divergent quantity is no longer sufficient': the square of the point-split product carries a universal divergence plus a STATE-DEPENDENT divergent cross term 2 C_uv (phi phi)_ren (their Eq. 5); they renormalise via the Hollands-Wald OPE, with coefficients scaling as 1/|sigma|^(8-i) (App. A) -- the same 8 as C3's r^-8. This confirms that divergences occur at coincidence and sharpens the tree's narrowing: the POINTWISE variance needs OPE-level renormalisation, not only the Sec. 3.2 counterterm cancellation; it says nothing against finiteness of a worldline-smeared variance.

later_literature.ref: Hu & Verdaguer 0802.0658 itself, p.80 (citing Hu & Phillips [8] and Hu & Roura [354])
later_literature.what: 'the noise kernel smeared over the horizon is divergent, and so are the induced metric fluctuations'. Smearing does not cure the coincidence divergence in every geometry of smearing: a null 3-surface smear still diverges. The tree's finiteness claim is for a TIMELIKE WORLDLINE (noise.py:207-210), where C4 shows finiteness in flat vacuum; the horizon remark is a caution for anyone extending the tree's claim to hypersurface or null smearing, not a contradiction of it.
later_literature.read_status: READ (p.80 page text); Hu & Roura [354] NAMED-NOT-READ

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result: the statement is a structural fact about the short-distance singularity of a free field's two-point function; no measured datum enters (data_at_publication: none). What was lacking in 2001/2008 was not data but a DEMONSTRATION in the review -- H&V assert the divergence and defer the pointwise limit (p.25). That gap is closed here in the flat massless vacuum by explicit computation (C3: coefficient 3(30 xi^2 - 10 xi + 1)/(2 pi^4), nonzero for every real xi), and by later work that renormalises the coincident product and finds its divergence (Perez-Sudarsky 2025/26, via the Hollands-Wald OPE). Evidence is AGAINST M's hypothesis for this result: nothing learned since moves it, and later work sharpens it (state-dependent divergent pieces for non-vacuum Hadamard states). The one defect found is notational -- a factor-4 normalisation mismatch between the review's Sec. 3.2 and Sec. 5 -- recorded as a discrepancy, not an error, and it cannot change whether a limit diverges.
grade_evidence: READ at source (0802.0658 p.29, verbatim; primary Phillips & Hu gr-qc/0010019 p.9-10, identical text). The tree uses the sentence exactly as published -- 'H&V Sec. 5.2.1 say divergences do occur in the coincidence limit' (noise.py:206-207) -- only to narrow its own earlier claim, and keeps the linear-field hypothesis (noise.py:202, 222-224). Re-derivation agrees: H&V's functional (5.29)-(5.32) reproduces an independent Wick computation exactly, and the flat-vacuum N_0000 goes as r^-8 with a coefficient nonzero for all real xi, so the pointwise limit diverges while the i*eps worldline smear is finite. No datum enters. Recorded, not grading: (a) a factor-4 normalisation discrepancy between Eq. (3.11) and Eq. (5.17) in the review; (b) the tree's gloss 'about SEPARATED points' paraphrases the source's 'meaning only in the sense of distributions'; (c) the re-derivation covers flat massless vacuum only, and the curved Hadamard extension (universal leading singularity) is NAMED, not run.
what_would_change_the_grade: To NARROWED: a Hadamard state or a curved background (within H1-H4) where the leading coincident singularity of N cancels -- not possible if the leading Hadamard term is universal, but that argument is NAMED here, not computed; or the tree extending the sentence to interacting or nonminimal fields beyond H1. To OPEN on the curved case: if a reader requires the curved coefficient to be computed rather than argued from the universal Hadamard singularity. No move to WRONG is in view: that would need a finite pointwise coincidence limit of N for a free field, and C3 computes the opposite.
